title: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope is the same between any two points on a line

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope is the same between any two points on a line
questions.prompt: Two slope triangles are drawn under the line. Explain why they give the same slope.
questions.prompt_markup: Two slope triangles are drawn under the line. Explain why they give the same slope.
questions.correct_answer: The triangles are similar (they have the same angles), so their rise-to-run ratios are equal: 2/3 = 2/3.

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope is the same between any two points on a line
questions.prompt: The points (2, 1), (5, 3), and (11, 7) lie on one line. Find the slope using (2, 1) and (5, 3), and again using (5, 3) and (11, 7). Explain why the two results must agree.
questions.prompt_markup:
The points (2, 1), (5, 3), and (11, 7) lie on one line.
Find the slope using (2, 1) and (5, 3), and again using (5, 3) and (11, 7). Explain why the two results must agree.
questions.correct_answer: 2/3 and 4/6 = 2/3. The two slope triangles are similar, so rise ÷ run is the same.
questions.grading_note: Grade both slopes and the similar-triangle reason.

questions.skill: Use similarity transformations to decide whether triangles are similar
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: On the line through (0, 1), (3, 3), and (9, 7), slope triangle T1 has vertices (0, 1), (3, 1), (3, 3). Slope triangle T2 has vertices (3, 3), (9, 3), (9, 7). Describe a translation followed by a dilation that maps T1 onto T2.
questions.prompt_markup:
On the line through (0, 1), (3, 3), and (9, 7), slope triangle T1 has vertices (0, 1), (3, 1), (3, 3). Slope triangle T2 has vertices (3, 3), (9, 3), (9, 7).
Describe a translation followed by a dilation that maps T1 onto T2.
questions.correct_answer: Translate T1 3 units right and 2 units up, so (0, 1) → (3, 3), (3, 1) → (6, 3), (3, 3) → (6, 5). Then dilate about (3, 3) with a scale factor of 2: (6, 3) → (9, 3) and (6, 5) → (9, 7).
questions.grading_note: Any correct sequence that names the translation, the center, and the scale factor is accepted.
